summary: Yiu Wing Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from The University of Hong Kong by 2013, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv University, Hanazono University under Sojo Hirano and Ben-Ami Scharfstein, and earned a PhD from Kyoto University. He was a professor at the University of Haifa (~1975–2003).
Yohei Kawajiri is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as a JSPS special research fellow (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda (born 1955) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Hisataka Ishida. He was a researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).

Yoneo Ishii (1929–2010) worked in history, archaeology, and religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Chulalongkorn University (~1957–1959), he served at Sophia University, became professor emeritus at Kyoto University, president of Kanda University of International Studies (~1995–2001), and CEACS director.
Yong Hua is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tengchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries, and served as lopön at Menri and Triten Norbutse, as well as visiting scholar at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Palpung Sherabling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under teachers including Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and became abbot of Palpung Sherabling Monastery around 1994.
Yongshan He is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at McMaster University under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Tsinghua and Harvard universities under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Irving Babbitt. His posts included professor at Southeast, National Central, and Peking universities, where he also served as vice-president.

Yonten Gyatso (1933–2002) was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned a Geshé degree from Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a diploma from École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he also served as research advisor for Tibetan Studies.

Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Sakurabe, held assistant and teaching posts at Kyoto, Kobe Women's, and Bukkyo universities, and served as professor at Otani University and Bukkyo University.

Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, later holding positions at the University of Tokyo, Toho Kenkyukai, Toyo Bunko, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He earned his doctorate at Komazawa University, studying under Shoson Miyamoto and Shigeo Kamata, and later served at Komazawa University as lecturer (1971) and professor (2001).

Yoshihiko Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and director of psychological operations at Kongoju (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University and a researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Center for Kyogaku and Dendo (attested 2003).

Yoshihito Muroji (born 1954) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, held posts at Kyoto University and Koyasan University, and was a professor at Shiga University of Medical Science.

Yoshinobu Kimoto (born 1950) is a historian and Japanologist. He studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. His posts include associate professor at Yonezawa Women's Junior College, president of Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and professor at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).

Yoshinobu Sakaide (1934–2020) was a scholar in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1953–1960) under Mitsuji Fukunaga (~1957–1963) and held a post at Kansai University (~1980–2005).

Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1933–1946) and held professorial posts at Kyoto University (1959–1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1978–1988).
